Privacy by Design for Gen AI: PII Redaction, Data Minimization, and Consent
Last Monday we introduced model and prompt cards so changes are transparent and safe. This week we will harden user trust by building privacy into the system from the start.
Trust is not a feature you ship later. It is a discipline you apply at every request.
Introduction
Gen AI systems can accidentally expose sensitive data if you do not design for privacy. A simple set of patterns keeps personal information protected without slowing teams down. In this guide we will focus on three pillars you can implement today: redaction, minimization, and consent.
Why Privacy First
•
Legal and policy risk drops when sensitive data does not reach the model input in the first place.
•
Users engage more when they know what is stored and for how long.
•
Incidents are easier to contain when you can prove that raw PII never left your boundary.
The Three Pillars
1) Redaction before inference Scrub inputs and tool results before they reach the model. Replace matches with typed placeholders so workflows still run. Examples: email, phone, credit card, address, government ID.
2) Data minimization by default Send only what the model needs for the current task. Avoid entire documents when a single paragraph will do. Keep scratchpads tight and use short lived caches.
3) Consent and transparency Tell users what you collect, why you collect it, and how long you keep it. Provide a clear forget option and make it easy to export or delete records.
The Three Pillars
Regex set, pick what applies
Email: (?i)[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,} Phone: (?:(?:\+?1)?[ .-]?)?(?:\(?\d{3}\)?[ .-]?)?\d{3}[ .-]?\d{4} Card: \b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,19}\b Replacement format: [TYPE_REDACTED]
Server side filter pseudocode
text := input text := redact(email_regex, text, "[EMAIL_REDACTED]") text := redact(phone_regex, text, "[PHONE_REDACTED]") text := redact(card_regex, text, "[CARD_REDACTED]") pass_to_model(text)
Copy and Use: Minimization Prompts
Use these system messages to keep outputs small and safe.
Only use information present in the provided context. If the answer requires data not present, say you do not have it. Keep responses under 120 words. Do not include personal identifiers.
Return valid JSON only. Keys: answer, citations, pii_detected (boolean). If pii_detected is true, do not include the detected value. Summarize without sensitive details.
Data Flow Checklist
•
Inputs pass through a redaction filter before the model.
•
Retrieval adds only the top passages needed, not entire documents.
•
Logs store hashes or tokens for sensitive fields, not raw values.
•
Caches are tenant scoped and expire quickly for any content that might carry PII.
•
Response traces include policy_version and privacy_flags for audit.
Common Pitfalls and Quick Fixes
•
Missed formats in regex rules. Fix by adding country specific phone and ID patterns and test them weekly.
•
PII in screenshots or images. Add an OCR step before redaction or block images for sensitive workflows.
•
Leaking data through citations. Display titles and stable IDs instead of raw snippets when necessary.
•
Confusing consent. Use plain language, a clear toggle, and a visible delete option.
Try It Now
1.
Add a server side redaction step to your chat endpoint and log the count of replacements per request.
2.
Cap your scratchpad to two hundred lines and rotate with summaries.
3.
Add a privacy section to your prompt and model cards with owner, last review date, and TTL rules.
Conclusion
Privacy by design is a set of habits, not a one time project. With pre inference redaction, strict minimization, and honest consent you will reduce risk, increase trust, and make future rollouts easier to approve.
